docs.text: Hello, welcome to my automotive docs project. I am a technical writer with over five years of experience documenting ADAS features for in-vehicle touchscreens using legacy tools. My plan is to create my own version of ADAS documentation, starting with Surround View Cameras, and host the content on its very own static site! This project is a work-in-progress that I'm working on daily. The goal is to apply the skills I've learned in information architecture and user experience and apply them to the docs-as-code process.

docs.text: Surround View Cameras Overview The surround view camera system uses front, side, and rear cameras to create a top-down view of your vehicle on the touchscreen. This view helps you maneuver your vehicle in situations like parking or moving out of a tight space. Precautions Warning The surround view camera system is meant to be a visual aid. Do not use the cameras as a replacement for checking your surroundings and driving with due care and attention. Failure to follow this instruction could result in property damage, personal injury, or death. Warning Use caution when adjusting vehicle settings while the vehicle is not in park (P). Failure to follow this instruction could result in property damage, personal injury, or death. Camera Locations Camera type Location Front camera Front grille Side cameras Side view mirrors Rear camera Rear bumper Using the Surround View Camera System Accessing the Surround View Camera Press the camera button on the touchscreen to access the camera display screen. You can also access the camera system using the menu on the touchscreen: Press the Settings button at the bottom of the touchscreen. Press Driver Assistance. Press Surround View Camera System. Switch Surround View Camera System on or off. The display shows the top-down view on the left side of the screen and the chosen camera view on the right side of the screen. Switching Between Camera Views Press the drop-down button on the top of the touchscreen. You can switch between the following views: Camera view What it does Front view Provides a view of the area directly in front of your vehicle. Front wide view Provides a widened 180 degree view of the area in front of your vehicle. Rear view Provides a view of the area directly behind your vehicle. Rear wide view Provides a widened, 180 degree view of the area behind your vehicle. Hitch view Provides a close-up view of the area around your tow hitch. Trailer view Provides a view of the trailer behind your vehicle. Note Rear view and hitch view are available at all speeds in reverse (R), drive (D), and neutral (N). Additional Views Your vehicle may be equipped with specialty camera views. Use the menu on the touchscreen to switch additional views on and off: Press the Settings button at the bottom of the touchscreen. Press Driver Assistance. Press Surround View Camera System. Switch the chosen view on or off. Turn Signal Views When you use your turn signal, the corresponding camera view appears on the touchscreen to aid you when checking your blind spot. The view disappears after you complete the turn or when you place the stalk back in its original position. Top-Down Truck Bed Views This view provides a top-down view of your truck bed to ensure any cargo or tools are secure when driving or while in park. Surround View Camera Limitations The surround view camera system has the following limitations: The top-down view is a combination of several camera views stitched together. The image may appear warped or distorted at the points where these views are combined. Dirty or blocked lenses can obstruct the camera view. Clean all camera lenses of debris, dirt, mud, or inclement weather to ensure an unobstructed view. The system is meant for flat surfaces. Using the cameras on steep inclines, curbs, speed bumps, or uneven terrain can make obstacles look closer or farther than they are in reality. Bright glare at dawn or dusk can wash out the camera view. Sudden lighting transitions like entering or exiting a dark tunnel can wash out or darken the camera view.
